properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-23, thinking out loud about how reflow2 should express its own decomposition.

HIS WORDS: "I want express reflow2 as 10 subsystems. Then say one of the subsystems is A and say there are 5 components associated with subsystem_A. They should be 'nested' as something like subsystem_A.component_1, subsystem_A.component_2, and so on. If component_2 [has] 3 sub-components, it'd be subsystem_A.component_2.sub_component_1."

⭐ MEASURED THE SAME DAY, AND IT CHANGES THE QUESTION: THE TEN SUBSYSTEMS ALREADY EXIST. reflow2 declares exactly 10 Components at `level: subsystem` (sys:agent-surface, sys:coherence-loop, sys:documentation, sys:foundation, sys:human-channel, sys:intake, sys:store, sys:time-history, sys:vocabulary, plus cmp:packaging), and ZERO components sit outside one — every component is parented on the CONTAINS spine. `req:recursive-black-box-decomposition` already requires nesting 'as deep as the design needs', and `Component.level` already carries the rung. So the STRUCTURE he is describing is built and populated.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN is narrower and it is about IDENTITY, not shape: should the path through the spine be expressible as an ADDRESS a person can read, write and search by? Today `cmp:detect` says nothing about where it sits; you learn that by walking CONTAINS.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STAND:
(a) DERIVE the path on read — a computed `path` field on any component, never stored. Cheap, cannot go stale, and it is a pure projection, which is what this project already demands of views. COUNTER: it is not an identity, so you cannot address a node by it, and two components with the same leaf name in different subsystems still collide in search.
(b) STORE the dotted id — `sys:coherence-loop.detect`. Reads exactly as he wrote it. COUNTER: an id that encodes position BREAKS THE MOMENT SOMETHING MOVES, and `cap:a-component-can-be-moved-not-just-given-another-parent` was built three days ago precisely so parts CAN move. This option makes the id a lie every time that capability is used.
(c) DO NOTHING — the spine is the answer and an address is a rendering concern.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether anybody needs to ADDRESS a node by path, or only to SEE the path. Those want different answers, and nothing measured says which is wanted.

⚠️ ONE ANOMALY FOUND WHILE MEASURING, worth its own look: `cmp:packaging` is at `level: subsystem`, contains NOTHING, provides nothing and consumes nothing — a subsystem with no inside. It is also the only one named `cmp:` rather than `sys:`.
properties.name: OPEN — should a nested part have an ADDRESS (subsystem_A.component_2.sub_component_1), or is the containment spine enough?
properties.rationale: Recorded via the brainstorm skill at `proposed`. Split from the contract-level and capability-composition questions he raised in the same breath, because each can be answered without the others.
